answer: Because the vault height is fixed at intake and logged in the tide receipt, the ripple audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 465 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 21 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
